body:

I tried deleting and reinstalling the app hoping it would fix the crashes, and I lost months of data and dozens of customised habits I had setup.

If you lose or have to change your phone, or if you delete the app, beware that your data isn’t saved in the cloud and you’ll be starting fresh! 😬😬

SUPER disappointing for such an expensive subscription. 

If iCloud back up (and syncing between devices) gets fixed I might consider changing my rating, but it’s still pretty buggy and laggy even without...

Edit: so glad I just found other alternative apps at similar or better prices. “Daily planner” and “done” seem A LOT more user friendly. I’d been holding out waiting for the problems with this app to be fixed... but I’m now glad to be cancelling my subscription and be rid of this app :)

title: Terrible interface design. Canceled after 7 days
body:
This app just didn’t work for me on my iPhone 6s, with the current iOS. It is pretty crazy how hard it was to just mark off when you have completed a goal or habit. The interface would mostly do everything except what I was trying to do. 

I’ve never experienced anything this badly designed on an iPhone app before. I’ve used a lot of different habit apps and none of them ever made it difficult to mark off a completed item.

Sliding the item on your list to the right is supposed to bring up the numbers to select how many times you have completed the item. 

Trying to get this to work in reality was incredibly frustrating. It keeps going to the calendar, it was too easy to accidentally Skip the item and I was always having to undo...it would go to a different page...everything except let me mark it as completed!!!!

There’s no option for challenges like Taking a break from alcohol to configure it to automatically mark the day as successful. This meant that every time I forgot or gave up trying to use the frustrating interface- I got a failure message and had to start again.

Cancelled after trying to use for 7 days. I’m a developer with 17 years experience in interaction design. Can’t believe this passed any user testing. Appalling design.

I’m a very visual person but bullet journals; post it notes or calendars stopped working a long time ago ago. Recently, due to depression , I felt the need to be more organized and productive and unfortunately Ive not been able to stay focused on the most simple things .. other apps can have all these reminder options or visual aids and etc however what I like about this one particularly is the fact we can: 
- allocate a certain amount of time for each habit 
- still tick it off as complete even without setting the timer (sometimes i forget to start a timer and by the time I’m done with a task I can just tick it off)
- having a timer on while you’re doing specific things allows you to understand the amount of time you spend on that activity and makes you focus more on it than if you just had a reminder And after a few days you start planing what tasks to do first based on the time you need for them so you’ll get into routines without forcing yourself into stuff as it happens with planners. 
- the fact you can have sounds on and off while the timer is on is cute. I don’t feel the need to get sounds for meditation so far as there’s some sounds in the app already.
Unfortunately I’m on the free trial and can’t  afford it yet but I can’t wait to see the graphs and all my activity laid out like that. Also be able to have multiple habits laid out. 

Thank you!

I understand the aim of making such an app with in-app purchases is to make a profit, but this is unbelievable. Limiting a habit tracking app to only five habits? Ridiculous. If you don't intend on coughing up for the subscription, I recommend that you give this extremely-restricted free version of an amazing app a pass.

The reason I can’t give a glowing review for Productive is because of the subscription model. How can anyone think that almost $2/month is value for money for the functionality provided? Granted it would take a little time to get the user interface to look as nice as this, but this is about as basic as a application can get! I wrote the pseudo code and coded up a functional framework for this in less than a day, since I like the concept but refuse to support a subscription model where it’s not justified.

Subscription models should be applied when new functionality and improvements are released on a regular basis. Talk about age of decadence.

title: What I've been looking for!
body:
I've been searching for the longest time for an app to help me manage my daily routines. 
As a parent of small children trying to stay productive at home and work, routine is key. I've searched high and low for a task management app that allows me to set routine tasks for certain days so I don't have to juggle everything in my head. Dividing the day into morning, afternoon and evening and specifying the time allows me to manage my day between morning, work and after work without having a cluttered tasks list. Although it's not its intended purpose it's the perfect system for managing the routine lifestyle of a working parent. 
My only criticism is I would like to be able to also use it to manage one off tasks and add them to specific days. Currently I have to use a separate app for that. 

Love the interface and design.

title: You should switch to Productive...
body:
Honestly. This app is fantastic. The minimalist layout looks fantastic, the swipe to complete, skip or add a new task is intuitive and smooth and the stat tracking keeps you motivated to keep using it! 

I dropped wonderful life for this app to manage my simple routines and activities and it's been fantastic. Currently my only other app used for productivity is Omnifocus due to it's ability to handle projects separate from actions and convert one to the other. However I'm not sure that's a feature I would want integrated here anyway, considering how well productive does the keep it simple approach and how daunting omnifocus is to get started with. 

Overall If I was asked to recommend a single app to help someone sort out task management and productivity, It's this one without a doubt!
